title: The Kingdom Is Still Blossoming
prayer: Lord, remain close to me. When I wander, draw me back. When I cannot see You, help me recognize the traces of Your grace around me. Let me feel Your warmth and direction, and use even my imperfect life for Your purpose. Your Kingdom is still growing. Let something of it grow through me. Amen.
body:
Paul was watching something extraordinary happen. The first Christian communities were beginning to blossom, but they were still filled with very human people. They divided themselves, followed personalities, questioned one another, and sometimes lost sight of Christ. Paul continually reminded them: I am only a servant. We are all instruments. God alone gives the growth.

How remarkable that after two thousand years, we are not so different.

Christian communities have multiplied across the world, yet the human heart still struggles with the same things. We divide, misunderstand, wander away, return, and try again. And somehow, despite us, God continues to give the growth. Perhaps perseverance itself is one of His quiet gifts.

Then Jesus tells us exactly why He has come: “I must proclaim the good news of the Kingdom of God, because for this purpose I have been sent.”

The crowds want Him to remain with them, but He cannot stay in one place. The Kingdom must keep moving outward—to another town, another person, another generation. Eventually it moved through Paul, through those imperfect early communities, through countless generations of believers, until somehow it reached us.

That thought makes Christ feel remarkably close.

We did not walk beside Him through Galilee. We did not hear His human voice or watch Him heal the sick. Yet the Kingdom He proclaimed that morning is still being proclaimed today. We are living inside the continuation of something He began.

And perhaps we are still imperfect instruments through which He carries it forward.
